findings.impact: TF-023D-003 code fix (replacing hardcoded pending_021J with dynamic lookup) is behaviorally correct but untested as an explicit assertion. findings.mitigation: Add a test function test_log_attribution to tests/scp_mcp/test_tools/test_consult_scorecard.py that: (1) creates a tmp_path with a docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub containing only comments (no active key entry), monkeypatches project_root to tmp_path, calls tools._resolve_audit_key_id(), and asserts the return value is 'key-ring-unreadable'; (2) creates a second case where docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub does not exist at all (file absent) and asserts 'key-ring-unreadable' again. findings.claim: DISPATCH-NOTE risk surface §2 says the fallback sentinel is 'pending_021J' but the code uses 'key-ring-unreadable'. Specifically: 'Mitigation: try/except wrap with fallback to "pending_021J" on read failure; logs INFO not ERROR.' The implemented fallback is 'key-ring-unreadable' (tools.py line 444: return "key-ring-unreadable"). An operator reading the DISPATCH-NOTE to understand the audit log behavior would expect key_id=pending_021J on key-ring read failures, but will observe key_id=key-ring-unreadable.
findings.evidence: docs/reviews/WP-SCP-023/dispatches/023E-threshold/DISPATCH-NOTE.md line 69: 'Mitigation: try/except wrap with fallback to "pending_021J" on read failure; logs INFO not ERROR.' src/standards_control_plane/mcp_server/tools.py lines 433-444: _resolve_audit_key_id returns 'key-ring-unreadable' on ValueError/OSError/AttributeError. The fallback value 'key-ring-unreadable' is more informative and correct than reintroducing the placeholder it was intended to replace, so the code is better than the DISPATCH-NOTE describes.
findings.impact: Documentation coherence gap. No functional impact since the exception is caught and not surfaced to callers. However, any log-parsing or audit tooling built to the DISPATCH-NOTE spec would filter on 'pending_021J' and miss 'key-ring-unreadable' entries.
findings.mitigation: Update DISPATCH-NOTE.md risk surface §2 to read 'fallback to "key-ring-unreadable" on read failure' replacing 'fallback to "pending_021J"'. Alternatively, note in a comment in the code that the fallback sentinel was deliberately chosen to be distinct from the old placeholder.

findings.claim: DISPATCH-NOTE describes USER-GATE-D as a '4-criterion checklist' in two places, but the actual docs/gates/USER-GATE-D.md has an 8-criterion checklist (criteria i through viii). The DISPATCH-NOTE 'Scope decision — IN' table row for USER-GATE-D says 'Lists the 4 criteria as a checklist; signs off when satisfied.' The slice acceptance criterion (iii) says 'docs/gates/USER-GATE-D.md exists with status not-yet-signed + 4-criterion checklist + operator-signature stub.' Both references are factually incorrect.
findings.evidence: docs/reviews/WP-SCP-023/dispatches/023E-threshold/DISPATCH-NOTE.md line 33 (Scope decision IN table): 'Lists the 4 criteria as a checklist'. DISPATCH-NOTE.md line 56 (Slice acceptance (iii)): '4-criterion checklist'. docs/gates/USER-GATE-D.md lines 18-25: 8 criteria present — (i) adopters, (ii) aggregator run, (iii) markdown report, (iv) MCP method live, (v) CODEOWNERS, (vi) TF-023D-003 closed, (vii) cross-repo notification, (viii) forward-filed TF health. plan-doc §8 Threshold A lists 5 criteria; USER-GATE-D adds (vi)-(viii) beyond the plan-doc and also adds (v) CODEOWNERS (implicit in plan-doc but not enumerated). The gate is more rigorous than the DISPATCH-NOTE describes.
findings.impact: An operator reading the DISPATCH-NOTE acceptance criteria to verify the slice would look for a 4-criterion gate and find 8 — a discrepancy that could cause confusion about whether the gate is correct. The extra criteria ((vi)-(viii)) add legitimate sign-off requirements beyond what the plan-doc §8 names explicitly: TF-023D-003 closure, cross-repo notification, and TF health state. These are defensible additions but were not described in the DISPATCH-NOTE as scope.
findings.mitigation: Update DISPATCH-NOTE.md in both references to say '8-criterion checklist' instead of '4-criterion checklist'. No change needed to USER-GATE-D.md — the 8-criterion content is correct and appropriate.

findings.claim: TF-023D-003 is code-complete (pending_021J placeholder replaced with dynamic lookup) but the key ring is operationally empty. Every MCP tool call therefore logs key_id=key-ring-unreadable rather than an actual key ID. USER-GATE-D criterion (vi) states 'TF-023D-003 closed. _log_tool_invocation reads the active key_id from docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub (replaced pending_021J placeholder).' The code reads from the key ring correctly, but since the key ring has no provisioned key, the 'active key_id' semantics of the criterion are not operationally achievable until the operator runs 'scp-mcp-server keygen'.
findings.evidence: docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub lines 1-6: file contains only comments — 'Operator generates the operational keypair post-merge via: scp-mcp-server keygen --out ~/.config/scp/mcp-signing-key. Public key, key-id, and rotation date are committed here once generated.' No ssh-ed25519 lines present. tools.py lines 905-936: _current_signing_key_id iterates lines matching _SIGNING_KEY_LINE_PATTERN; with no matching lines it falls through to raise ValueError. tools.py lines 433-444: _resolve_audit_key_id catches ValueError and returns 'key-ring-unreadable'. Therefore all tool calls currently log key_id=key-ring-unreadable. USER-GATE-D criterion (vi) says 'TF-023D-003 closed' — this is listed as a checkable criterion before signing, but operationally requires a keygen step that must happen post-merge.
findings.impact: The audit log will continue to show key_id=key-ring-unreadable for all MCP tool calls until the operator provisions the key ring. USER-GATE-D criterion (vi) cannot be checked off by reading the logs alone — the operator must first run keygen, commit the public key to docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub, and redeploy. This dependency is undocumented in the USER-GATE-D or DISPATCH-NOTE.
findings.mitigation: Add a note to USER-GATE-D.md criterion (vi): 'Note: key ring provisioning is an operator step post-merge — run scp-mcp-server keygen, commit the public key to docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub, and redeploy the MCP server. Criterion is checkable once key_id values appear in the MCP audit log.' This makes the operational dependency explicit without blocking Threshold A sign-off on the code change.

findings.claim: _current_signing_key_id raises ValueError with messages that say 'provision a key ring before using propose()' in all three code paths (file not found, OSError, no active key found). Now that this function is called from _resolve_audit_key_id for ALL MCP tools (not just propose), the error message is misleading when triggered from consult_rules, check_waiver, etc.
findings.evidence: tools.py lines 907-936: three ValueError raise sites, all with message 'signing key ring not configured at docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub; cannot record signing_key_id - provision a key ring before using propose()'. _resolve_audit_key_id (line 433) catches this ValueError and returns 'key-ring-unreadable' without surfacing the message to any caller. The message is only visible in internal exception context. It is not logged or returned to MCP clients.
findings.impact: Zero functional impact — the message is caught before surfacing. Developer confusion if debugging _current_signing_key_id failures in non-propose contexts.
findings.mitigation: Optional: update the three ValueError messages to say 'provision a key ring before using MCP tools' or make the message context-neutral. Low priority; acceptable to defer to next maintenance pass on tools.py.

summary: CORRECTNESS R1 review of WP-SCP-023 023E at HEAD 2883087. Two MAJ findings block approval. COR-MAJ-001: STATUS.md 023E chain row is absent from the 'Today's chain (2026-05-03)' table, and the 023D row still shows 'this' instead of '#100'; DISPATCH-NOTE acceptance criterion (vi) names both the 023E chain row and Threshold A follow-up as required — only the follow-up was delivered. COR-MAJ-002: DISPATCH-NOTE names 'test_log_attribution' as a delivered test and acceptance criterion (iv) says 'Tests confirm'; no such function exists in test_consult_scorecard.py; the _resolve_audit_key_id fallback path has no explicit test assertion. Three MIN findings: COR-MIN-001 DISPATCH-NOTE risk surface says fallback sentinel is 'pending_021J' but code uses 'key-ring-unreadable' (code is more correct; doc is stale); COR-MIN-002 DISPATCH-NOTE says '4-criterion checklist' but USER-GATE-D has 8 criteria (gate content is correct; description is wrong); COR-MIN-003 USER-GATE-D criterion (vi) references 'active key_id' which is not operationally achievable until the operator provisions the key ring (key ring currently empty). Two nit findings: full SHA not independently git-verifiable at review time; _current_signing_key_id error messages reference propose() in non-propose contexts. All positives: SHA prefix match confirmed; opt-in-registry SHA is an exact byte-for-byte match with the wrapper; USER-GATE-D content (8 criteria, sign-off stub, post-signoff actions, not-yet-signed status) is correct; _resolve_audit_key_id fallback logic is correct; no pending_021J functional references remain in tools.py; consult_scorecard registered in tools set; regression analysis clean.
